study_identification.title: Dissecting Heterogeneity in Functional Network Connectivity Aberrations in Antipsychotic Medication-Naïve First Episode Psychosis Patients - A Normative Modeling Study

study_characteristics.study_objective: Characterize inter-individual heterogeneity in resting-state functional network connectivity and test whether normative values can help identify biologically less heterogeneous subgroups of antipsychotic-naïve first-episode psychosis patients.

dataset_name.answer: Normative model trained on ~22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (2–100 years); local healthy controls used for calibration.
dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states the approximate size and age span of the normative reference and that in-study HCs were used for calibration.
dataset_name.supporting_text: The normative model was generated using resting state connectivity data from approximately 22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (age range (yrs): 2-100). Healthy control data collected in this project were used for calibration of the normative reference curves.

analysis_level.supporting_text: Functional brain networks were then parcellated using the Yeo-17 functional network parcellation atlas ... resulting in a functional connectivity matrix of 136 connectivity values.

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FSL BET; FSL topup; CONN toolbox (21a); ART; aCompCor; ANTs (as-needed registration correction); band-pass 0.008–0.08 Hz; 4 mm FWHM smoothing; no global signal regression.

Outlier volumes were censored using the ART toolbox ... aCompCor ... Global signal regression was not performed ... ANTs was used to correct the registration mistakes.

deviation_metric.reason: Statistical analyses section defines z-scores and the ±2 SD binarization threshold.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: We quantified functional connection deviations expressed as standard deviations (z-score) ... We binarized z-scores ... cut-off value of ±2 standard deviations.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Subgrouping by deviation profiles (positive-only, negative-only, mixed, none); FDR control (alpha=0.05); significance threshold of ≥4 deviations; subgroup vs overall similarity compared via z-test.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Functional network pathology is highly heterogeneous; deviation-based subgroups are less heterogeneous than the overall patient group.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: No more than 11.1% shared positive deviations and 8.3% shared negative deviations in the same connection. Forty-eight percent had no deviations. Deviation-defined subgroups showed reduced heterogeneity (positive subgroup: z = -2.88, p = 0.002; negative subgroup: z = -3.36, p < 0.001).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Normative reference likely overrepresents European ancestry, mismatching patient demographics; caution warranted when transferring models to diverse data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Global signal regression was not performed; deviation mapping may support precision-psychiatry subgrouping despite similar clinical presentations.

general_notes.general_notes: Preprint on medRxiv (not peer-reviewed). Acquisition: Siemens 3T Prisma; two rs-fMRI runs with opposing PE; Yeo-17 atlas; connectivity matrix of 136 edges; ART censoring (>0.9 mm motion or >5 SD global signal); exclude if mean FD >2 mm or >50% censored; aCompCor nuisance regression; band-pass 0.008–0.08 Hz; 4 mm FWHM smoothing; ANTs used if registration issues; no global signal regression.
